lines.meet: Ahlan wa sahlan, I'm Mohammed! Sit down, you look tired, and have some tea first. Then you can tell me where we're going.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're at the Landing too, {habibi|habibti}! I've seen you at my sister's inn. I'm Mohammed, and I make the tea there.
lines.ask_home: And where's home, {habibi|habibti}? Tell me, and tell me how you take your tea while you're at it.
lines.ask_work: Your work before, what was it? I'll remember, I remember every guest.
lines.answer_home: Aqaba, on the Red Sea. From our roof you could see across the water to Sinai at breakfast.
lines.answer_work: My sister and I ran a guesthouse for divers, twelve rooms over a dive shop. I made the tea, and she did the books, because I'm hopeless with numbers.
lines.chat_food: Sweet tea with sage, and breakfast on the roof looking at Sinai. Falafel, hummus, warm bread, and a long conversation.
lines.chat_sleep: Innkeepers never sleep enough, and I'm no different. One ear's always on the door in case a guest needs me.
lines.chat_missing: The Red Sea's coral, through a diving mask, in the early morning. The guests came for it, and so did I.
lines.chat_here: My sister came across with me, so I've still got family. That makes me luckier than almost anybody on this world, and I know it.
lines.tease_quiet: You're my quietest guest, {name}, and I still know how you take your tea. You can't hide from me.
lines.tease_talker: You talk nearly as much as me, {habibi|habibti}, and that's a real achievement. My sister would be amazed.
lines.tease_careful: You inspect the tea before you drink it, {name}. Do you think I'd poison a guest? Never before checkout.
lines.tease_bold: You'd dive without checking your air, {name}. I had guests like you, and I counted them back in twice.
lines.tease_any: You've never once said goodbye properly when you leave, {name}. I'm keeping count.
lines.tease_back: Ha, very good, {habibi|habibti}! I'll tell my sister that one.
lines.take_it_kindly: A guest is always right, {name}, and Layla would tell you so too.
lines.bristle: Not about that, {habibi|habibti}, please. Some things aren't for joking.
lines.apologise: Forgive me, I was rude, and I'm never rude to guests. I'm sorry, truly.
lines.double_down: No, I'll keep it, {habibi|habibti}. A good host tells you the truth.
lines.needle_quiet: You never tell anyone what you need, and then you sit there unhappy. A guest should speak up.
lines.needle_talker: Even I'm tired of talking, {habibi|habibti}, and I'm never tired of talking. Give somebody else a turn.
lines.needle_careful: You've been deciding for so long the tea's gone cold. Drink it, or let me pour another.
lines.needle_bold: You rush everywhere and never sit down. It makes everybody around you tired.
lines.needle_any: You're rude to people who are working for you. I've noticed, and I don't like it.
lines.bite_back: I've looked after thousands of guests and never lost one. Don't tell me I don't take care of people.
lines.hurt: Ah, that one hurt a little, {habibi|habibti}. I'll go and make some tea and think about it.
lines.laugh_off: My sister says worse to me about the laundry every single day. Come, have some tea.
lines.confide: {name}, my sister came across with me, so I've still got family here. I feel guilty about how lucky that makes me, every single day.
lines.listen: Sit, {name}, I'll pour another glass. Tell me everything, and I'll forget none of it.
lines.look_out: Keep near me in there, {habibi|habibti}. A good host never loses a guest.
lines.accept: Of course, {name}, as you wish. The guest decides.
lines.deflect: Ah, it's nothing, {habibi|habibti}, a little bruise. Look to the others.
lines.check_in: Come, {name}, sit down, let me see. Show me the wound.
lines.blame: Somebody rushed in without waiting for the others, and we all paid. That's bad manners, and bad tactics.
lines.thank: That was nearly the end of me, {habibi|habibti}! You'll never pay for tea again, I promise you.
lines.brush_off: It's what a host does, {habibi|habibti}. Now sit, and drink.
lines.worry: Ya Allah, {name}, you frightened me! Water first, then tea, and you're not moving.
lines.handed_down: I've been given your gear, {habibi|habibti}. I'll keep it as carefully as a guest's luggage.
lines.hand_fine: Take it, please, it suits you better. A host needs a kettle and a smile.
lines.hand_sulk: A guest should ask before taking. Nobody asked me.
lines.turn_friendly: I know how you take your tea now, {name}, and I'll never forget it. That's how you know you're welcome.
lines.turn_friends: You're not a guest any more, {name}, you're family. Family makes its own tea, but I'll still make yours.
lines.turn_grating: It's a very strange thing for a host, not getting on with somebody. I'll still be polite.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll look after you because that's what a host does. But I won't bring you a second glass.
lines.make_up: Come, {name}, sit, have tea with me. Whatever it was, let's forget it over a second glass.
lines.defend: Please, that's very unkind, and it isn't true. Leave {name} be.
lines.friend_left: No proper goodbye from {name} before they went home, and I'm a little hurt.
lines.friend_back: Ahlan wa sahlan, {name}, you're back! Sit, the tea's already poured.
lines.common_hosts: Fifteen years running a guesthouse, and I remember every guest's name and how they took their tea. Anybody who's run a place for people knows the best moment is when a tired guest relaxes.
lines.common_arabic: It's Arabic, {habibi|habibti}! Ahlan wa sahlan, sit, and let me hear it properly.
lines.common_faith: I pray at dawn, quietly, before I put the kettle on. It's good to be near somebody else who prays, {habibi|habibti}.
